scope: WPF public HP meter and committed damage/recovery feedback
changes: SeatTemplate includes a static current-HP meter, preserving the existing health icons and numeric label.
Low HP uses a warm warning color; negative and over-limit values are clamped only in the visual fill.
The existing battle layer paints a short receding damage remainder and highlights recovered HP.
HP delta, remaining HP and current public maximum come from committed public event projection and player-safe presentation data.
Only the latest applicable HP result paints a trail. New maximum, motion off, reset and reload do not replay stale tracks.
Scaled-seat overlays use the rendered meter's transformed inner track.
Effects preview uses the same HP control and shared frame clock as the table.

filters: declaration and general library views protect private faces

boundaries: Red damage remainder visibly shrinks, then retires.
Rapid recovery removes the old red remainder.
A change of maximum invalidates a trail from the old maximum.
Critical, dying, zero maximum, large maximum and over-limit inputs remain inside the track.
HP automation name reports the public value and maximum.
Half-scale remainder geometry matches the actual static bar and avoids protected command areas.
Animation rendering and cold load preserve native command history and all four safe viewer snapshots.

limits: Native command fixtures prove damage/recovery boundaries; their placeholder generals and fixture skill banner are diagnostic data.
No foreground physical keyboard/mouse, audio or multi-monitor DPI acceptance.
The half-scale geometry check is a WPF transform check, not physical multi-DPI acceptance.
Rapid damage/recovery floating numbers can still overlap; observed in health-track-recovery.png and prioritized for the next iteration.
Transient trails currently follow DamageAppliedEvent and RecoveryAppliedEvent; other HP/max changes keep an immediate static track.
Routine is 135.937 seconds, above the approximately one-minute target.
No manual full verification, release/publish, commit or push.

cleanup.reason: Prior exact-path deletion blocked by policy; no automatic retry. Exact reused paths remain registered.
